proposition.claim:
Equation reference: eq:energy, eq:h3, eq:spectral. The torus has normalized Lebesgue measure and its usual quotient metric. For an actual pointwise kernel \(W\), the paper defines \[
 \mathcal E_W[\rho]=\frac12\iint_{\mathbb T^d\times\mathbb T^d}
 W(x-y)\,d\rho(x)\,d\rho(y).\] The hypotheses on p. 4 require \(W\) to be integrable, even, lower semicontinuous and bounded below (H1), with zero mean and strictly positive nonzero Fourier coefficients (H2), and \[
 \frac1{|B(x;r)|}\int_{B(x;r)}(C_1+W(y))\,dy
 \le C(C_1+W(x))\] for some constants and every ball (H3). The additional lower bound is \(\widehat W(k)\ge c|k|^{-d+s}\), \(k\ne0\), with \(s<d\). Theorem 1.4 derives energy stability from the asserted identity \[
 \mathcal E_W[\rho]=\frac12\sum_{k\ne0}\widehat W(k)|\widehat\rho(k)|^2,\] which is equation (1.12) on p. 3. For \(d=1,s<0\), the conclusion is \(d_\infty(\rho,1)\lesssim \mathcal E_W[\rho]^{1/(2-s)}\). Theorem 1.6 on p. 5 then asserts the same control for any minimizer of \(\mathcal E_{\widetilde W}\), replacing the energy by \(\|W-\widetilde W\|_{L^\infty}\).

Recorded check: Integral energy at delta0 is0, spectral expression pi²/6, distance to uniform1/2. For nu=(delta0+delta1/2)/2 energy=-pi²/24<0. Independently Wtilde=K except Wtilde(0)=-pi² has essential-sup difference0 and delta0 attains the global lower energy bound -pi²/2.

d=1,s=-1,rho=delta0. W=K except W(0)=0; K=2pi²(x²-x+1/6) periodic. H1 holds by downward semicontinuous modification; H2 and quantitative lower bound c=1 hold because W_hat(k)=k^-2. H3 holds with C1=1+pi²/6,C=1+pi²/2, since 1<=C1+W<=C.

repair.content:
Restricted L2-density repair via Young and Parseval proved in report. Pointwise bounded perturbation repair verified conditional on valid base all-measure energy bound. Full arbitrary singular-kernel repair not asserted.

Keep R^(-d-1)(1+log R), which is L1. Periodization gives L1 bound; Schwartz Fourier sum gives Linfinity; interpolate.
